title: Diary entries & messages
examples: Should I start my entry with the date or the greeting?
What kind of feelings should I write about to make it sound real?
Is it okay to use slang in a diary entry?

explain.say: Today we are learning to write diary entries and messages. These are personal writings for yourself or a friend.
When writing in a diary, you must use the first person. This means using words like I and me. You are writing as yourself.

items: I went to the park today.

explain.say: Good entries often talk about feelings. You can say if you were excited or maybe a little bit sad. Feelings make writing interesting.
The format is important for a message. You need a clear greeting and a sign-off. This tells the reader who wrote it.
For a real-life example, imagine you are writing to your best friend. You might start with 'Dear Maya' and tell her about a fun game you played.
A common mistake is forgetting the date in a diary. Always include the date so you know exactly when you wrote it.

faq.q: Do I have to write about my feelings every time?
faq.a: No, you do not have to write about your feelings every single time. You can write about events that happened instead.
asks: Is it okay to skip feelings?

faq.q: What is the difference between a diary and a letter?
faq.a: A diary is for yourself, so it is private. A letter is for another person, so you address it to them.

faq.q: Should I use full sentences or can I use short notes?
faq.a: It is best to use full sentences to make your writing clear. This helps your reader understand exactly what you mean.
asks: Can I write in short bits?

faq.q: If I write a message, do I need a closing like 'Bye'?
faq.a: Yes, a closing helps your friend know the message is finished. You can use 'Bye' or 'See you later'.
asks: How do I end a message?
Do I need a goodbye word?

faq.q: Can I write about things that happened last week?
faq.a: Yes, you can write about things from the past. Just make sure you include the correct date for when you are writing it.
asks: Does the date have to be today?

facts: Diary entries record personal events and thoughts.
Messages are written to communicate with another person.
First person writing uses 'I' and 'me' to tell stories.
A good format includes a date and a clear greeting.

quiz.say: Which sentence uses the first person correctly?
quiz.show: I saw the big blue butterfly.

options.show: The big blue butterfly saw me.
options.say: The big blue butterfly saw me.

options.show: I saw the big blue butterfly.
options.say: I saw the big blue butterfly.

options.show: He saw the big blue butterfly.
options.say: He saw the big blue butterfly.

quiz.why: This sentence uses 'I', which is the first person pronoun, showing you are telling your own story.

wrong.0: This changes the focus and does not keep you as the main person telling the story.
wrong.1: This misses the subject, so the reader does not know who did the seeing.
wrong.3: This uses 'He', which is the third person, making it sound like someone else saw it.

quiz.say: If you are writing a message to your teacher, what is the best greeting?
quiz.why: A formal greeting like 'Dear' followed by a name is appropriate when writing to a teacher.

wrong.0: This greeting is too casual for a teacher and might seem disrespectful.
wrong.1: This looks more like an envelope label than the start of a message.
wrong.2: This is very informal and should only be used with close friends.

quiz.say: What must you include at the very top of a diary entry?
quiz.why: The date helps you remember exactly when you wrote down those thoughts and events.

wrong.0: This describes a feeling, but it does not tell the reader what day it was.
wrong.2: This is a statement, not a date, so it does not help you remember when you wrote it.
wrong.3: This is the greeting, which comes after the date, not before it.
